summary: Use the existing static vanilla-JS app as the baseline. Round 4 is a focused UX/layout pass: keep clipboard parsing, 6-candidate generation, preference-point behavior, save/load, and swap editing intact, but move the saved-player loader into a separate side area, add a collapsed-by-default toggle, compress each saved player into a one-line row, and make the full row hit area selectable without reintroducing numeric score UI.

milestones.title: Sidebar Layout Refactor
milestones.objective: Reposition the saved-player loader so it no longer extends vertically under the main input flow, and add collapsed-by-default panel state without disturbing the rest of the app shell.
deliverables: Refactor `src/lib/render.js` `renderShell()` so the top workspace becomes a two-column layout on desktop: left column for paste/input controls, right column for the saved-player loader and supporting sidebar content.
Move the saved-player section out of the current full-width position below the main grid and into the sidebar area, while keeping `preview` and `result` panels in the main flow below.

Add `savedPanelExpanded` state to `src/main.js`, default it to `false` on first render, and wire a toggle control that expands/collapses the saved-player body without affecting current roster or results state.
Update `src/constants/copy.js` with Korean labels and helper text for the new folded/unfolded UI, including a compact header summary when the panel is collapsed.

Update `src/styles.css` with explicit sidebar layout classes, collapsed/expanded panel styling, and a responsive fallback that stacks the sidebar below the input area on narrower widths without changing the default collapsed behavior.

milestones.title: Saved Player Row Simplification
milestones.objective: Replace the existing saved-player card/list hybrid with a compact, name-first selection row that can be scanned quickly and selected from anywhere in the row.
deliverables: Rewrite `renderSavedPlayers()` and the per-player row markup in `src/lib/render.js` so each saved player renders as a single compact row with name first, then compact inline tier/preference summary, selection state, and a delete action.

Make the selection hit area cover the visible row body, including text and empty row space, instead of relying on a small checkbox target. If a checkbox indicator is kept, it should be decorative or secondary to the row click target.
Keep individual delete and clear-all actions available, but isolate the delete control so clicking delete does not also toggle row selection.
Add a capped-height scrollable list container in `src/styles.css` so long saved-player libraries stay usable without stretching the page vertically.
Preserve exact-10 selection feedback in the toolbar so the user can always see `선택 n / 10` whether or not the list is expanded.

milestones.title: State Wiring And Flow Preservation
milestones.objective: Reconnect the new sidebar and row interactions to the existing load/save workflow without regressing optimization, editor behavior, or hidden-score rules.
deliverables: Update saved-player event handling in `src/main.js` so row clicks toggle selection, delete buttons remove records, clear-all resets selection state, and the collapse toggle only changes panel visibility.

Keep `load-selected-button` disabled unless exactly 10 saved players are selected, and keep the existing saved-player count/selection summary in sync after every toggle, delete, clear, save, and reload.

Preserve the current `loadSavedPlayersIntoMatch()` flow so loading 10 saved players rewrites the textarea with canonical TSV, hydrates `matchPlayers`, clears previous candidates/editor state, and shows Korean confirmation copy.

Do not change candidate ranking rules in `src/lib/optimizer.js`; this round is not an optimizer rewrite. The existing ordering by total diff, role-group diff sum, tank diff, then unranked diff must remain intact.

Keep the main UI free of numeric balance-score output after the layout refactor. Candidate cards, current roster, and editor should continue to hide per-player score, team total, and numeric diff labels.

milestones.title: Regression Coverage And Handoff Docs
milestones.objective: Lock the new sidebar UX down with automated checks and leave the workspace documentation aligned with the shipped behavior.
deliverables: Extend `test/appFlow.test.js` to cover: collapsed-by-default initial render, expand/collapse toggle, full-row selection toggling, delete-without-select side effects, exact-10 gating, and load-selected reset behavior.
Update `test/responsiveLayout.test.js` so it asserts the new sidebar layout contract, saved-list scroll container, row-level compact styling hooks, and stacked layout fallback at smaller widths.

Keep or extend regression coverage for header/headerless parsing, candidate count 6, candidate uniqueness, swap editing, and hidden-score rendering so the round-4 UI work cannot silently break round-3 behavior.

If needed for the chosen implementation, update `testing/fakeDom.js` only enough to support the new row/toggle interactions; prefer simple ID-addressable controls over introducing broad fake-DOM complexity.

Update `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` to describe the new sidebar placement, default collapsed behavior, one-line row selection UX, and the fact that prior browser/mobile real-device verification remains documented as non-blocking for this iteration.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` as required verification. `npm run test:browser` remains optional evidence only; if it is not run, keep the docs truthful about that.

acceptance_criteria: On first load, the saved-player loader renders in a side area separate from the main paste/input area and starts in a collapsed state.
The saved-player panel has a visible fold/unfold control in Korean, and toggling it expands/collapses only that panel body.
When collapsed, the saved-player panel does not render as a long vertical section under the main input flow.
When expanded, the saved-player list uses its own capped-height scroll area instead of growing the whole page indefinitely.
Each saved player is shown in one compact row with name-first presentation and inline summary data instead of a tall detailed card layout.
Clicking the saved-player row body, including text and empty row space, toggles that player's selected/unselected state.
Clicking the per-row delete control deletes that player without also toggling its selection state.
The saved-player toolbar count updates immediately after selection, deselection, individual deletion, and clear-all deletion.
`선택한 10명 불러오기` remains disabled unless exactly 10 saved players are selected.
Loading exactly 10 saved players rewrites the textarea with those 10 players, hydrates the current roster, and clears prior candidate/editor results until recalculation.
Saving the current valid roster still persists tier data and role-preference point data to local storage.
Individual saved-player deletion still works after the layout refactor.
The clear-all saved-player action still removes the entire saved-player library and resets selection count to `0 / 10`.
Header-present and headerless paste input both still parse correctly.
The app still renders exactly 6 candidate combinations for a valid 10-player roster.
Every candidate still satisfies `1탱 2딜 2힐` per team and does not duplicate a player within that candidate.
Candidate ordering still follows total score difference, role-group score-difference sum, tank score difference, and unranked distribution difference, with randomness only inside fully tied buckets.
Selecting a candidate still loads it into the final edit area, and two slot clicks still swap players immediately.
The main UI still hides personal numeric scores, team totals, and numeric score-difference labels by default.
All new saved-player sidebar, toggle, and status copy is shown in Korean.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` describe the shipped sidebar/collapse workflow and explicitly treat prior browser/mobile real-device verification gaps as non-blocking for this round.
test_strategy: Extend `test/appFlow.test.js` to assert initial collapsed state, toggle behavior, row-body click selection, delete-button isolation, exact-10 gating, and load-selected roster hydration/reset flow.
Update `test/responsiveLayout.test.js` to check for the new sidebar layout classes, saved-list scroll container, compact saved-row styling hooks, and mobile-width stacking fallback.
Retain parser regression coverage for both header-present and headerless TSV input so the layout work cannot break the ingestion flow.
Retain optimizer/editor regression coverage for 6 candidates, no duplicate assignment, required ordering, candidate selection, and two-click swap behavior.
Add or retain render-level assertions that forbidden score labels do not appear anywhere in the main UI after the saved-player refactor.

If the row-click implementation needs different interaction primitives, make the smallest possible `testing/fakeDom.js` change and keep tests centered on public UI behavior rather than internal DOM structure.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` before handoff. Treat `npm run test:browser` as optional, and only claim it in docs if it was actually executed.

risks.risk: Moving the saved-player section into the sidebar can accidentally break the current page hierarchy or push important panels below the fold in awkward ways.
risks.mitigation: Use an explicit top-level two-column shell in `src/lib/render.js` and `src/styles.css`, keep preview/result panels in their existing main flow, and add responsive layout assertions for both desktop and narrow-width stacking.

risks.risk: Making the whole saved-player row clickable can create event collisions where delete also toggles selection, or where only part of the row is actually interactive.
risks.mitigation: Implement the row selection target and delete target as clearly separated controls, and add app-flow tests that click both paths independently to prove the behavior.

risks.risk: The compact one-line row can overflow badly with long Korean names or dense tier/preference summaries.
risks.mitigation: Use `min-width: 0`, truncation/overflow rules, and a capped scrollable list container; verify the CSS contract in `test/responsiveLayout.test.js`.

risks.risk: The layout refactor can unintentionally regress round-3 functionality such as exact-10 load gating, swap editing, or hidden-score rendering.
risks.mitigation: Do not rewrite app-flow or optimizer logic beyond the saved-panel wiring, and keep regression tests for candidate generation, selection, swapping, and hidden-score text in place.

risks.risk: A junior builder may accidentally treat the sidebar work as a reason to modify ranking or expose internal balance numbers for debugging.
risks.mitigation: State explicitly in the plan and acceptance criteria that `src/lib/optimizer.js` ranking rules stay unchanged and that score numbers remain internal-only.

risks.risk: Collapse state can get reset or lost during partial re-renders, leading to confusing UX when the user saves, deletes, or loads players.
risks.mitigation: Keep `savedPanelExpanded` as a top-level state value in `src/main.js` and ensure all panel re-renders read from that single source of truth.

risks.risk: Docs may overclaim browser/mobile verification status because prior QA artifacts flagged that area.
risks.mitigation: Update `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` to describe only the verification actually run in this round and explicitly note that real-browser/mobile evidence is non-blocking here.

definition_of_done: The saved-player loader is rendered in a side area, not as a full-width vertical section under the input flow, and it starts collapsed by default.
The saved-player panel can be expanded/collapsed in Korean UI without affecting current roster, candidates, or editor state.
Expanded saved players render as compact one-line rows with name-first scanning and full-row selection hit area.
Saved-player selection, exact-10 load gating, individual delete, and clear-all delete all work correctly after the UI refactor.
Clipboard parsing, role-preference editing, save/update, 6-candidate generation, candidate selection, and two-click swap editing all still work.
Candidate ordering rules and hidden-score UI rules remain unchanged.
Automated coverage verifies the new sidebar UX plus key existing flows, and both `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` reflect the shipped round-4 workflow and the non-blocking browser/mobile verification stance.
open_questions: Assumption: the saved-player panel should default to collapsed on every fresh page load and does not need its open/closed state persisted in local storage.
Assumption: the delete button is intentionally excluded from the row-wide selection hit area; every other visible part of the row should toggle selection.
Assumption: the one-line saved-player row may use abbreviated inline tier/preference summaries or truncation as needed, as long as it remains clearly scannable and avoids tall multi-line cards.
Assumption: on desktop, the saved-player loader should live in the right sidebar next to the paste/input area; on smaller widths it may stack below that area while remaining collapsed by default.
Assumption: no optimizer or preference-ranking changes are required in round 4 beyond regression coverage; the main scope is saved-player UX and layout.
Assumption: existing browser/mobile real-device QA gaps from prior rounds are not blockers for this iteration, but the docs still need to report verification status accurately.
Assumption: the current `현재 10명 저장/업데이트` entry point remains in the current-roster section; round 4 only changes how saved players are browsed and loaded, not where saving is initiated.
